action.question: How aggressive should the restart be?

questions.question: How aggressive should the restart be?

options.label: Just merge + restart supervisor (Recommended)
options.description: Fast-forward main + kickstart supervisor. Existing mini-*/oneoff-* servers keep old argv until natural turnover. Zero session loss.

options.label: ...also bounce the 5 mini-* servers
options.description: After the supervisor restart, kill the 5 mini-* PIDs so the supervisor respawns them with bypassPermissions. Any active inner sessions on them get disconnected.

options.label: Bounce everything mm-* AND oneoffs
options.description: Maximal cutover. Kills ~65 servers including ~60 oneoff worker sessions. Lost work for whatever's running. Only do this if you know nothing important is in flight.

transcript_tail.text:
Filed and on the board.

- **#42** [\[AH\] perm-gate scans commit-message bodies and blocks legitimate risky-op descriptions](https://github.com/jdtogni78/ai-harness/issues/42) — Status: **Todo** on project #2

The body lays out three fix options (exempt opaque payload flags, scan the staged diff instead of the message, or document the workaround) with #1 as the recommendation, plus a reproducer and a cross-reference to commit `f805982` where it was first hit. The `--dangerously-skip-permissions` deny rule is explicitly called out as out-of-scope so a future fix doesn't accidentally weaken it.
Did we restart the sessions? Let we restart all the... launch these, make sure it picks up the new code.
Let me check what's actually running first, since "restart all" has different cost depending on what's where.

Before I touch anything, one critical check — the supervisor runs from `/Users/claudio1/dev/ai-harness` (per `PYTHONPATH=/Users/claudio1/dev/ai-harness` in the perm-gate hook config). Our commit `f805982` is on the bridge worktree branch, not on whatever `~/dev/ai-harness` is checked out to.

Found the gap. Here's what's actually running and what each step costs:

| Component | State | Picks up new code by... |
|---|---|---|
| Main checkout `~/dev/ai-harness` | on `main` @ `1039593` (no f805982 yet) | merging the worktree branch to main |
| Supervisor (PID 6746, launchd) | running on `main` code | `launchctl kickstart -k` after main is updated |
| 5 `mini-*` per-dir servers (mm-* equiv) | argv shows `acceptEdits` | bouncing each one (supervisor respawns in ~30s) — **kills active inner sessions on those servers** |
| ~60 `oneoff-mini-*` servers | argv shows `acceptEdits` (1 already on `bypass`) | natural turnover (supervisor doesn't respawn oneoffs) — **bouncing them kills the worker sessions running on them** |
| Manager-ui | not running on this host | next time it starts |
| `titles-monitor`, `usage-monitor` | running, unaffected | n/a (don't touch perm modes) |

**Critical:** the supervisor doesn't know about our commit yet — `~/dev/ai-harness` is on main. Restarting it now without merging first would just reload the same old code.

Proposed plan (least-disruptive, gets the new default live without killing anyone's work):

1. Fast-forward `~/dev/ai-harness` main to `f805982` (local merge from the worktree branch — no push)
2. `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.claudio1.claude-remote-control` to reload the supervisor with the new code
3. **Don't bounce the 5 `mini-*` servers** — they keep their old `acceptEdits` argv until they idle-recycle (~12h) or get bounced for unrelated reasons. New `mini-*` spawns (e.g. on supervisor adopting a new active-dir) immediately use `bypassPermissions`.
4. **Don't touch the ~60 `oneoff-*` servers** — those are active worker/human sessions; killing them = losing work in progress.

Things deliberately not in this plan:
- **Push to origin** (you didn't ask, and the other host `note` isn't in play here)
- **Bouncing the `mini-*` servers** (cheap option: just let them recycle. Aggressive option: bounce them now — say the word if you want this, but I'd want to see if you have anything running on any of them first.)
